d1m1-role.lead: Case Management is the **end-to-end coordination, tracking and handling** of a case, from intake to resolution.

concepts.text: Every file passes three tests: **timely progression**, proper documentation and compliance, effective communication
more: Timely progression of cases: no file sits without **a dated next step**
Proper documentation and compliance: every contact, document and deadline in the CMS
Effective communication between all parties: client, carriers, providers and Atty. Thorne

concepts.text: Keep the file's status current and summed up, so **Atty. Thorne decides** from one read
Research **the relevant laws and rules**: deadlines, notice requirements and the state's own conditions
Draft, name and file **every legal document** to the firm's standard, for Atty. Thorne's signature
Watch **task compliance and case progress**: every task done on time, every phase moving
more: Task Compliance Monitoring: each task has an owner and a date
Case Progress Monitoring: the file moves **phase by phase**, never stalls

concepts.text: Keep John Doe informed and directed; **log every contact** the same day
Read the whole file for risk, not single tasks: **spot the weak point** early
more: The usual weak points: **a missed deadline**, a silent client, a gap in treatment
Flag it to Atty. Thorne the day you see it, with the facts and a next step

concepts.text: Allocate the file's resources and **recommend next steps**; strategy itself stays with Atty. Thorne
more: Resource Allocation: the right provider, vendor and task at the right time
Planning and Recommendation: you draft the plan; **Atty. Thorne sets strategy**

framework.title: The General Process

steps.label: Intake & Case Opening
steps.text: Verify the facts, run the Conflict Check, **open the file** in the CMS

steps.label: Case Planning & Strategy Support
steps.text: Draft the Case Plan and recommend next steps; **Atty. Thorne sets strategy**

steps.label: Documentation & File Management
steps.text: Request, name and file every document; **the CMS** is the single source of truth

steps.label: Communication Management
steps.text: Keep the client, carriers and providers updated; **log every contact**

steps.label: Case Monitoring & Tracking
steps.text: Docket every deadline and **flag risk** to counsel the day you see it

steps.label: Billing & Documentation Support
steps.text: Keep **the bills, liens and costs** recorded and current for the demand

steps.label: Case Resolution & Closing
steps.text: Support resolution and disbursement, then **close a complete file**

framework.note: Seven steps on one track; each case phase, Intake to Litigation, has its own goals and deliverables.

d1m1-l1.lead: The Intake Phase is where Case Managers establish **control, structure and clarity** from the very beginning of a case.

concepts.text: Intake is the first chance to ensure **accuracy, compliance and proper case direction**
Verify and organize essential case information while ensuring the case **meets acceptance standards**
more: Capturing complete and accurate client details
Screening for **conflicts of interest**
Assessing case viability and eligibility
Establishing a properly structured case file

concepts.text: The first interaction with a potential client, **followed immediately by intake**
more: It gathers the basic facts and **assesses urgency**
It decides whether the case can move forward

concepts.text: Your role begins after intake: **quality control and case validation** before a case is accepted
more: Intake work is complete and accurate
It is properly documented
It is **ready for case activation**

concepts.text: Run in the system **before proceeding**, on every party's full legal name, and documented
Review every document for **completeness and relevance**; flag what is missing or inconsistent
Create the case file with **proper naming conventions** and a complete system entry
Run intake end to end yourself, then **communicate next steps clearly** to the client or team
more: Conduct a full intake call or review the intake submission
Identify **missing or inconsistent** client information
Perform and document a conflict check accurately
Decide if the case meets basic acceptance criteria
Set up a complete, organized case file in the system
Communicate next steps clearly to the client or internal team

framework.title: The Intake Workflow

steps.label: Inquiry Form Submitted
steps.text: The intake arrives; on this file, the raw file from **“On the Records”**

steps.label: Details Reviewed and Verified
steps.text: Check the DOL, parties and signatures against **the Police Report**

steps.label: Conflict Check Completed
steps.text: Every party's **full legal name**; log its date and result

steps.label: Approved or Escalated
steps.text: Complete intake moves to acceptance; **uncertain eligibility** goes to Atty. Thorne

steps.label: File Created and Logged
steps.text: Open the matter in the CMS: roles mapped, **SOL docketed**, documents named

framework.note: This phase determines whether the case should move forward or be declined.

d1m1-l2.lead: Before clinical planning, the **Regulatory Triple-Check** establishes the claim and your authority to act; the Payer Order then decides who funds care.

concepts.text: A payer's right to stand in the client's shoes and **recover what it paid** for accident care
more: On this file: **Peach State Health Plan** asserted a reimbursement right on first notice
Record carrier, member ID PSH-55017742 and group GRP-41208 in the lien register the same day
Flag it against the matter before the first demand is drafted
Registering a lien isn't conceding it; enforceability and any compromise are Atty. Thorne's

concepts.text: Deciding which payer is billed first, so each bill **goes to the right payer** and nothing is paid twice
more: 1. PIP/MedPay, if any applies: verify it, never assume
2. Private health insurance: here, Peach State Health Plan
3. LOP/provider liens, last
Not the Recovery Stack: the Payer Order pays the bills; **the $40,000 stack** pays the claim
Which payer is primary when policies conflict is Atty. Thorne's call

concepts.text: The firm's written promise to pay a provider from the settlement: **last in the Payer Order**
What the client keeps once fees, costs and liens are paid: **a late-flagged lien** comes straight out of it

framework.title: The Regulatory Triple-Check
head: Check
What you do
Why it matters
rows: Obtain a claim-specific authorization naming the incident date
A standard release may not be adequate for injury claims
If 65+ or on SSDI, report the case to the BCRC
Avoids federal penalties and **settlement freezes** under MMSEA
Set the Payer Order: PIP/MedPay → private health insurance → LOP/provider liens
Each bill reaches the right payer; reimbursement rights surface early
framework.note: Clear all three before clinical planning begins: the claim is established and you are authorized to act.

d1m2-l1.lead: The No Contact Protocol is a **formal due-diligence record**: it tracks silence, proves the firm tried, and protects it from liability.

concepts.text: Points where work slows, stalls or turns inconsistent; **a silent client** is one, delaying case progression
Proof the firm made reasonable, documented efforts to reach the client: **the record that justifies** whatever comes next
more: Log every attempt as you make it: **date, time, channel, outcome**
An unlogged attempt did not happen
Escalate by channel, not volume: two voicemails on one number clears the phone rung only
Step 3: notify Atty. Thorne, document it, assess the SOL and any hearing dates

concepts.text: The contact methods the client and firm agreed at intake; **only approved channels** count as a valid attempt
more: The ladder: 2+ phone attempts → email and text → emergency contact → certified mail or letter
Step 1 confirms every earlier attempt used **an approved channel**
Give the client an easy way back: a call window, a text, an upload link

concepts.text: A second person, collected at intake, who can **still reach the client** after they go quiet

framework.title: Common Intake Bottlenecks
head: Bottleneck
How it shows up
rows: Missing contact details or incident facts; no supporting documents
**Unanswered clarification requests**, missed verification calls, slow documents
System backlog, incomplete entries, unclear opposing party information
Incorrect dates, inconsistent statements, missing signatures, misfiled records
Ambiguous facts of loss or liability needing attorney review
Incomplete intake packets; miscommunication between departments
framework.note: A silent client is Delayed Client Follow-Up: the No Contact Protocol clears it, one logged attempt at a time.

d1m2-l2.lead: The Final Warning Letter **closes the outreach record**: one last documented notice before the firm searches for the client or counsel moves to withdraw.

concepts.text: Certified mail proves delivery; email gets a response. **Each covers the other's gap**
more: Confirm the current address first: a letter to **a stale address** proves nothing
Same letter both ways: earlier attempts itemized with dates, a 7–14 day deadline, withdrawal notice
Keep the certified receipt; log both channels in CMS → Documents → Outgoing

concepts.text: An AND gate, not a checklist: the search waits until **all three are true**, so money isn't spent early
more: 1. Contact ladder exhausted: phone, email, text and emergency contact, all logged
2. Final Warning Letter sent by certified mail AND email
3. Its 7–14 day deadline has passed with no contact
Then escalate to Atty. Thorne with **the complete log** attached

concepts.text: A paid search for a missing person's current address and contacts; **counsel authorizes it** because it spends firm money
Ending representation by Notice of Withdrawal or Motion to Withdraw; **only the attorney decides**, under firm and court rules
more: The letter may say withdrawal is possible, **never that it's happening**
Never write “we are withdrawing” in a letter the attorney hasn't approved
Only the attorney decides, and tells the client, that representation is ending

framework.title: The No Contact Protocol, Steps 4–6

steps.label: Final Warning Letter
steps.text: Earlier attempts itemized, a 7–14 day deadline, withdrawal notice; certified mail AND email

steps.label: Decision Point
steps.text: Still no response: **the attorney decides** on a Notice or Motion to Withdraw

steps.label: File Closure
steps.text: Marked “No response – withdrew per protocol”; proof of every attempt retained

framework.note: Skip-tracing waits for all three: ladder exhausted, letter sent, deadline passed. Counsel authorizes it.

d1m3-l1.lead: Client instructions protect the claim from **the client's own good intentions**: what the client says, posts, signs or skips can become evidence.

concepts.text: A medical danger threatens the client's health; a legal danger, like **a gap in care**, threatens the claim
more: The client starts treatment and keeps every appointment
Barriers (transport, cost, work) reported to you **before a visit is missed**
Explain the process, not the stakes: what a missed visit means is Atty. Thorne's to explain

concepts.text: Everything on the file can reach defense counsel, so instructions stay **factual, never legal opinion**
The notice that the firm represents the client; from then on, adverse contact **routes through the firm**
more: No Recorded Statement to the adverse carrier: all adverse contact routes through the firm
The one carve-out: the adverse carrier may discuss **Property Damage only** with the client
If a Property Damage call turns to injuries, treatment or the facts of loss, it stops and routes to the firm
Log every adverse contact in CMS → Communications Log

concepts.text: Every accident-related cost needs its receipt or trip log: **only what is documented** can be recovered
more: Every receipt for an accident-related out-of-pocket expense
Mileage to and from appointments
Household help
Log each expense in CMS → Case Notes the day the client mentions it

d1m3-l2.lead: Property Damage is **the owner's separate claim**; for a passenger's injury case it is evidence of the impact, and sometimes a date that reaches care.

concepts.text: PD follows the vehicle: it belongs to **the owner's claim**, not to a passenger who owns no car
Photos, estimates and supplements show the force: **proof of impact severity** for the injury claim
Where an owner's PD date reaches the client's care, **calendar it and plan around it**
Questions on the owner's rental, Loss of Use or value **go to the attorney**, logged the same day

framework.title: Property Damage Severity and the BI Roadmap
head: Case phase
What the PD shows
How it strengthens BI
rows: Tow from the scene, airbags, crush photos
Flags a serious injury early; **preserve the evidence**
Major structural impact, frame or pillar damage
The force matches the injuries the providers record
**Answers the low-impact defense** before it is raised
The same photos and repair figures, on file
Keeps the injury claim from being called minor
Physical proof for experts and trial
framework.note: The PD claim stays the owner's; its severity is **physical evidence** for the injury claim in every phase.

d1m4-l1.lead: Early evaluation joins **coverage, liability and projection**: is there money, who is responsible, and how the case is likely to move.

concepts.text: Which policies apply, with what benefits, limits and exclusions: **is there money** to pay the claim?
Who caused the incident and to what degree: **clear, shared or disputed**, and on what evidence
more: Not final until confirmed by the Police Report, **the driver statements**, and any dashcam or other evidence
Ambiguous? Clarify the facts with the client, then escalate with a short summary of what's unclear
Never tell the client liability is a sure thing

concepts.text: An early read of risk and trajectory from coverage, liability, injury, treatment and documents; **value stays with counsel**
more: Reads coverage, liability, injury severity, treatment expectations and documentation quality
Preliminary until coverage is **confirmed in writing**; re-project when coverage changes
States risk and trajectory, never a figure, value or settlement posture

concepts.text: In a legal framework, Case Management shifts from **best efforts to strict compliance**: every plan deadline is docketed
more: File the Three-Pillar Case Plan within the state's window, **often 30 to 60 days**
Docket the filing window and route the plan to Atty. Thorne
Every action item gets an owner and a date; every pillar, measurable goals

framework.title: Why These Three Work Together
head: Element
The question
What you check
rows: Is there money to pay the claim?
Valid policies, coverage type, limits, exclusions and gaps
Who is responsible, and to what degree?
Who caused it; clear, shared or disputed; evidence; comparative negligence
How is this case likely to move?
Coverage, liability, injury severity, treatment expectations, documentation quality
framework.note: Projection reads risk and trajectory; it stays preliminary until coverage is confirmed, and case value stays with Atty. Thorne.

d1m4-l2.lead: A Case Plan is a **living, approved document**: drafted in structure, reviewed by counsel, then run.

concepts.text: One structure for every plan, so reviewers can **scan it fast** and nothing is missed
more: Five bands: snapshot & acceptance → coverage, liability, projection → Triple-Check → Three-Pillar Plan → risks
Owner and date in **their own fields**, not in a sentence
Adverse facts stated plainly in the risks band: a buried risk hasn't been disclosed

concepts.text: Draft, route, review, approve, execute; **a return is normal**, a step back into drafting, not a failure
more: Draft: edit freely; execute nothing that commits the firm externally
Routed: keep preparing internally; don't act on the plan's positions
Returned: address **every comment**, then re-route; never part-execute
Approved: execute against this version and record it as the operative plan
Superseded: a material fact changed after approval, so re-route

concepts.text: A conclusion still awaiting its proof; when the proof arrives and differs, **the plan is re-routed**
The CMS keeps every version unaltered, so **each approval is provable**, and every note is discoverable
more: Never edit a record in a way that breaks the trail
Keep treatment notes factual and clinical; strategy stays in the legal track
Never “this will help the case” in a treatment note

framework.title: Mandatory Disclosure & Compliance Tracking
head: Requirement
What the plan tracks
rows: A CMS that keeps an **unalterable audit trail** of every version
Carrier-mandated deadlines, such as an early IME in no-fault states
Providers treating under an LOP, so no bill arrives as a surprise
Medical plan and legal claim as parallel tracks: coordinate, don't commingle
framework.note: The file is discoverable in litigation: write every plan note as if defense counsel will read it.

d1m1-upl.lead: UPL is giving legal advice without a license; a Case Manager stays on **the fact side** of that line, every time.

concepts.text: Telling the client what a record says: a date, an amount, **what was sent**, and when
What happens next, what a form is for, and **who decides**; never how it ends
Any opinion on what his facts mean for **his rights, money or choices**: the attorney's alone
more: Never case value, legal strategy, or whether to settle
Never what a fact (a gap in treatment, **a prior injury**, a missed visit) does to the outcome or money
A kind reassurance about the outcome (“you'll be fine”) is still advice
The test: am I telling him what is, or what he should do?

concepts.text: An opinion question is written down word for word and **sent to Atty. Thorne** the same day
more: The routing line: “That's Atty. Thorne's call; I'll get it to him today”
Log his words exactly in CMS → Case Notes · Tasks
Tell him when to expect an answer, so routing never feels like **a brush-off**

d1m4-tplan.lead: Before a plan can be built, understand the **whole person**: more than the medical records. Then set defensible goals and map the interventions they need.

concepts.text: The person, not just the chart: assessment is **more than reviewing records**, and it comes before the plan
Physical, **cognitive and psychological** impairments, recorded as reported and documented, never diagnosed by you
more: John Doe at intake: “neck stiffness” on the EMS Run Report, and he **declined transport**
No treatment yet, so record his symptoms in his own words, with the date

concepts.text: Housing, family support, financial stability: **the barriers** that turn a plan into a Treatment Gap
more: He lives with his mother, Margaret Doe, at 2214 Maple Hollow Rd
He owns no car, and **Margaret's Civic** was damaged in the crash
Ask how he will reach care, and whether cost is stopping him

concepts.text: The client's baseline: it **separates a pre-existing condition** from an accident-related injury
more: Ask about every prior injury, treatment and claim, with dates and providers
**Request the prior records**; never leave them for the defense to find
Whether a prior condition was aggravated is the provider's opinion and Atty. Thorne's argument

concepts.text: Can the client return to the previous role, or will he **need retraining**?
more: Northgate Distribution warehouse shift lead since 01/12/2026
**$22.00/hour, 8-hour shifts**; record the job's physical demands in his words

concepts.text: In a PI file, goals must satisfy **clinicians and adjusters alike**: an objective measure and a date
Maps the specific interventions the goals need, in **four standard groups**
more: Acute/Restorative Care: surgery, physiotherapy, occupational therapy
Psychological Support: counseling or CBT for PTSD, anxiety or **adjustment disorders**
Durable Medical Equipment: sourcing wheelchairs, ramps or assistive technology
Rehabilitation Milestones: inpatient to outpatient to home-based care

concepts.text: Inpatient to outpatient to home-based care: **each transition** is where a gap can open
more: John Doe declined transport, so his care would begin as outpatient care
Calendar each handoff and **confirm the first visit** happened

framework.title: SMART Goal Setting
head: Attribute
What it means
In a PI case
rows: “Ambulate 50 meters with a rolling walker,” not “improve mobility”
A standardized scale an adjuster can verify
ROM %, ODI/VAS, FIM, PHQ-9, sessions attended
Realistic for the injury and the prognosis
The provider's prognosis sets the target, never the claim
Tied directly to the injuries claimed
Daily living and return to work
A clear milestone to review against
“By the 12-week review”; “ROM up 30% within two months”
framework.note: Defensible to clinicians and adjusters alike: the provider sets target and measure; the CM writes the goal into the Case Plan.

d1m4-tmap.lead: Mastering the Standard Treatment Map separates a Case Manager who **observes a recovery from one who drives it**: deviations trigger denials and IMEs.

concepts.text: The usual route of care after a crash, from EMS to long-term pain management, read **stop by stop**
more: Emergency response: EMS and the emergency room stabilize and assess
Diagnostics: MRI and radiology find the underlying injury
Rehabilitation: chiropractic care and physical therapy
Surgical interventions: orthopedics, pain management and, by severity, surgery and post-operative care
Long-term care: long-term pain management that sustains recovery and prevents relapse
A skipped or out-of-order stop needs **a documented clinical reason**

concepts.text: At each check-in one question, **“Is the patient improving?”**: yes continues the map, no opens the variance loop
more: Phase 1: verify PIP and put the mechanism of injury (MOI) on record
Phase 2: conservative care and imaging, with “Is the patient improving?” asked at every check-in
No: the variance loop. Medication or injections, an ortho or neuro referral, a psychological screen for yellow flags
Phase 3: work hardening, an FCE, and whether surgery is indicated
Phase 4, MMI: the impairment rating, final lien resolution, settlement support
Every branch is **the provider's decision**; you raise it and record the answer

concepts.text: When care drifts off the map, **diagnose the why** before the insurer stops paying for it
more: Clinical: a secondary complication, such as radiating nerve pain that wasn't in the first report
Psychosocial: yellow flags such as fear-avoidance, depression or no transport to therapy
Systemic: an insurer's delay authorizing an MRI or a specialist referral
The fix depends on the type: **a systemic delay is not non-compliance**

concepts.text: The utilization-review test: usual for the mechanism of injury, with **objective functional gain**, not pain alone
more: Reasonable: is the treatment common for this mechanism of injury (MOI)?
Necessary: is there objective evidence, not just reported pain, that function is improving?
Necessity is **the provider's opinion**, argued by Atty. Thorne; you put the measures on file

concepts.text: Adjusters look for a functional gap at week 6: expect **20–30% more range of motion** or less pain
more: Count the six weeks from the first visit, not from the date of loss
Pain is scored on the VAS, from zero to ten
Still 10/10 after 12 PT sessions? **Raise it with the provider now**
Don't wait for the adjuster to deny the next six sessions

concepts.text: No change in the disability index after 12 weeks of PT is **a plateau**: ask about a specialist
more: The map's answer to a plateau is a specialist or a second opinion, not more of the same
Whether to refer is **the provider's call**; you ask and record the answer

concepts.text: Standard measures that put recovery in numbers an insurer reads; **the provider chooses and orders them**
more: Oswestry (low back) or DASH (arm, shoulder, hand): disability in daily activities, every 30 days
Gait analysis: mobility and fall risk, for lower-extremity injuries
PHQ-9 / GAD-7: depression and anxiety screens, when physical progress stalls
FCE, the Functional Capacity Evaluation: before return to work or at MMI
A screen that puts mental health in the record is **flagged to Atty. Thorne**

concepts.text: You route information between clinic, counsel and payer; **one broken loop** can stall a case for months
more: Clinical loop: therapy notes match the physician's orders; “90% recovered” against “total disability” is a documentation crisis
Ask both providers to clarify a conflict and tell Atty. Thorne; **never resolve it yourself**
Legal loop: status reports to Atty. Thorne in functional terms, what he can't do at work and home
Financial loop: update the payer before a referral or authorization lapses, so a lapse isn't read as non-compliance

framework.title: The Standard Treatment Map
head: Phase
Timeline
Typical interventions
Case Management focus
rows: ER or urgent care, imaging (MRI/CT), bracing, RICE, initial PT
Active PT 2–3 times weekly, specialist follow-up
Monitoring functional gains: range of motion, weight-bearing
Identifying barriers to return to work
Permanent impairment rating; an FCE if ordered
Final lien resolution and settlement support for Atty. Thorne
framework.note: Every intervention is the provider's order; the Case Manager tracks the phase, spots the variance and asks.

d1m4-tcare.lead: Know the standard US treatment protocols so you can see **a deviation**: in the records as red flags, on the phone as yellow flags.

concepts.text: A deviation from standard treatment that signals **medical danger**, a stagnating case, or over-treatment for billing
more: Medical danger (fever, hardware failure) goes to the provider **the same day**
Legal danger (missed visits, generic notes) goes to Atty. Thorne
Once a flag is spotted, A-C-T runs: Assess, Coordinate, Track

concepts.text: PT is **the baseline of treatment**; its flags signal a case stagnating or over-treated for billing
more: Over 12 sessions with no range-of-motion or pain change, and no specialist or imaging suggested
Heat packs, TENS or massage with **no active exercise**: feel-good care adjusters discount
Two or more missed visits: the defense reads an injury not serious enough to treat

concepts.text: Surgery is a claim's most valuable element; its flags concern **safety and Standard of Care**
more: Surgery such as a spinal fusion before PT or injections, outside an emergency: **a Reasonable Necessity flag**
Left and right switched in the records: credibility damage at trial
“Just wait until the follow-up” for fever or redness: a malpractice concern
Sharp or mechanical pain after surgery may mean a loose screw or retained sponge; the provider hears it today

concepts.text: The most scrutinised area of care, under opioid regulations and **Medical Necessity audits**
more: Opioid + muscle relaxant + sedative, “the Holy Trinity”: a safety risk, and a liability if he has an accident medicated
Doses rising with no change in diagnosis: failing treatment or forming dependency
A drug screen without the prescribed drug, or with an illicit one: **facts to the prescriber**, never an accusation

concepts.text: High-value cases handled with **utmost discretion**: claims must be tied to the accident and validated
more: Notes on “general life stress”, not the accident's trauma: rarely covered, and costs challenged as unreasonable
No memory loss at the ER, then significant symptoms months later: **the provider validates** before anyone relies on it
Record the date each symptom was first reported, and tell Atty. Thorne

concepts.text: Psychosocial barriers that **derail the map**, heard in conversation more often than read in records
more: Fear-avoidance: avoiding movement or therapy for fear of pain
Catastrophizing: “I will never walk again” despite minor clinical findings
Litigation stress: conflict with the defense side slowing recovery
Iatrogenic factors: reliance on opioids, or on passive care (ice, heat) over **active exercise**
Whether a PHQ-9 or GAD-7 screen is indicated is the provider's call

concepts.text: Keeps a client committed when **the newness wears off**, by drawing out his own reasons to continue
more: OARS: Open-ended questions, Affirmations, Reflective listening, Summaries
Developing discrepancy: the gap between what he does now and **his long-term goal**
Rolling with resistance: don't argue, pivot: “That clinic isn't a good fit for you. Let's look at why.”
Boundaries prevent burnout; active listening means he feels heard

concepts.text: At the midpoint, excitement wanes and hard work begins; **adherence drops** unless someone re-engages him
more: Course correction: Assess Response, Evaluate Efficacy, Adjust Intervention
A client not reaching his goals: **usually the plan**, not the person
A plan change is proactive management, not an admission; the change itself is the provider's

framework.title: Treatment Red Flags by Specialty
head: Specialty
Red flag
What it signals
rows: Over 12 sessions, no range-of-motion or pain gain, no referral
Heat, TENS or massage only; no active exercise
Surgery advised before PT or injections, outside an emergency
Post-op fever, redness or sharp pain left “until the follow-up”
Opioid + relaxant + sedative; doses rising; a drug-screen mismatch
“General life stress” notes; head-injury symptoms first reported months later
Costs challenged; needs the provider's validation
framework.note: Medical danger reaches the provider the same day; legal danger reaches Atty. Thorne. Then A-C-T runs.

d1m4-emc.lead: PIP is written state by state. **The EMC rule is Florida's**: 14 days to initial care, and an EMC finding decides $2,500 or $10,000

concepts.text: First-party coverage paid regardless of fault, written **state by state**: limits, percentages and conditions change at the state line
more: Florida PIP: $10,000, paying 80% of reasonable medical expenses and 60% of lost income
Riverton PIP, John Doe's file: Harbor Point $5,000, paying 100% of medical and 80% of lost income
Riverton has **no EMC rule** and no 14-day condition

concepts.text: Acute symptoms, possibly severe pain, serious enough that **no immediate care** could seriously jeopardize health or bodily function
more: Acute symptoms of sufficient severity, which may include severe pain
Absent immediate care, expected to cause serious jeopardy to health, impairment of bodily functions, or dysfunction of an organ or part
Whether it exists is **the provider's clinical judgment**

concepts.text: Florida PIP pays no medical benefits unless initial care is received **within 14 days** after the accident
more: Count from the date of loss and docket the 14th day at intake
Hypothetical: a 02/06/2026 date of loss puts day 14 on **02/20/2026**, John Doe's first visit

concepts.text: An MD, DO, dentist, PA or APRN's EMC finding opens **the full $10,000**; without it, $2,500
more: A chiropractor may give initial care but **cannot make the finding**
Massage and acupuncture are not reimbursable under Florida PIP
Confirm the current statute: Florida has repeatedly considered repealing PIP
